\[
\beta = \max\!\left(1, \left\lfloor c \, \frac{M}{256} \right\rfloor\right),
\quad
\tilde{h}^{(t)}_k = \min\!\left(h^{(t)}_k, \beta\right) + \left\lfloor \frac{E^{(t)}}{256} \right\rfloor + r^{(t)}_k,
\quad
T^{(t)}(k) = \operatorname{round}\!\left(\frac{255}{M} \sum_{j=0}^{k} \tilde{h}^{(t)}_j\right),
\quad
I_{\text{out}} = \sum_{t} w_t(x, y)\, T^{(t)}(I),
\qquad
c = 2,\ 8 \times 8\ \text{tiles}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(h^{(t)}_k\): The number of pixels of tile t at level k
- \(M\): The number of pixels in one tile
- \(c, \beta\): The clip limit and the largest count a bin may keep
- \(E^{(t)}\): The number of clipped pixels of tile t
- \(T^{(t)}\): The curve of tile t
- \(w_t(x, y)\): The bilinear weight of tile t at the pixel

h^(t) is the histogram of tile t and M the number of pixels in a tile. No bin may hold more than beta pixels. The E^(t) pixels above the limit are spread over all 256 bins, the same share to each. The remainder r goes out one pixel at a time from bin 0, with a step of max(1, floor(256 / remainder)). The tile curve T^(t) is the scaled running total, rounded to whole levels. The slope of a tile curve at level k is 255 / M times the count of that bin, so the limit caps the contrast gain at about c. Each pixel blends the curves of the four nearest tile centers with bilinear weights w_t. Tile centers sit at the middle of each tile. Outside the outermost centers, the nearest curves are used. These are the steps of cv::CLAHE in OpenCV, which follow Zuiderveld. Values between two levels take each curve interpolated between them.
